screening.screening_rationale: Patient provides coherent, well-organized description of photo with adequate detail. Speech follows logical progression from foreground subjects to background, includes appropriate inferences about emotions and relationships. Minor disfluency ('It's and') falls within normal conversational patterns. No evidence of thought disorder across any TALD domains.

Single-word affirmative response (Yeah) is contextually appropriate for yes/no confirmation question from interviewer. Brevity matches question type and does not indicate poverty of speech. No thought disorder evident.

Patient provides logical explanation for inference about upset emotions, citing specific observables (facial expressions, body language). Makes reasonable interpretative leap to possible affair scenario. Minor disfluency (the what the) represents normal self-correction. No thought disorder present.

Patient provides systematic, coherent description of farm scene with multiple elements (landscape, people, activities). Information flows logically from general setting to specific details. Appropriate level of descriptive detail without vagueness or excessive elaboration. No thought disorder detected.

Patient provides direct, logical explanation for supervisor inference, citing specific observables (stance, hands on hips, authoritative appearance). Response is contextually appropriate and well-reasoned. Minor speech disfluency (the the) is common in spontaneous speech. No thought disorder present.

Patient provides coherent, systematic description of photo scene with multiple people and setting. Makes reasonable inferences about relationships (family, student, farm caretaker) based on visual cues. Utterance cut off mid-sentence due to interviewer time constraint, not thought disorder. No FTDs detected.
